t: 3570. Find Books with No Available Copies — Editorial
o:
## Understanding the problem
We have books with `total_copies` and borrowing records where `return_date IS NULL` marks a book currently borrowed. A book qualifies if the number of active borrows equals (or exceeds) its total copies, i.e. zero copies remain. In the example, *The Great Gatsby* has 3 active borrowers against 3 copies (available = 0) and *1984* has 1 borrower against 1 copy; both qualify, while *To Kill a Mockingbird* (2 of 3 out) does not.

Constraints imply a simple aggregate query: join, filter NULL returns, group by book, compare the borrow count with `total_copies`, then sort.
k: A book has zero available copies when COUNT of NULL-return records >= total_copies.
Filter return_date IS NULL before aggregating; GROUP BY book attributes.

a.i: Join each book to its unfinished borrowing records, count them per book, and keep only books whose active-borrow count reaches the total copy count. Sorting handles the required output order.
s: Inner join library_books to borrowing_records on book_id with return_date IS NULL.
Group by book_id and select COUNT(*) AS current_borrowers.
HAVING COUNT(*) >= MAX(total_copies) (or b.total_copies with proper grouping).
Order by current_borrowers DESC, title ASC.

c.python:
-- MySQL solution (problem is SQL-only)
SELECT b.book_id, b.title, b.author, b.genre, b.publication_year,
       COUNT(*) AS current_borrowers
FROM library_books b
JOIN borrowing_records r
  ON b.book_id = r.book_id AND r.return_date IS NULL
GROUP BY b.book_id, b.title, b.author, b.genre, b.publication_year
HAVING COUNT(*) >= b.total_copies
ORDER BY current_borrowers DESC, b.title ASC;

a.t: O(B + R log B) — one join plus aggregation/sort over records.

w: Use the join-group approach; a correlated subquery `(SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE return_date IS NULL)` also works but is usually slower. Pitfalls: forgetting the NULL filter, using `>` instead of `>=`, and grouping only by book_id in strict SQL modes. Follow-ups: return available-copy counts, or handle damaged/unborrowable copies.
